## [2026-10-14](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-14.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14423>)

This work fits multimodal pretraining laws that account for directional transfer, competition for model capacity and diminishing returns from repeated vision or audio data. Controlled mixture-of-experts experiments make the framework useful for planning how to divide a training budget among model size, unique data and modality mixtures, while requiring coefficients to be fitted for the intended setup.

**Published:** 2026-10-10 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:31.851Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Scaling Laws, Multimodal Pretraining, Data Mixtures

**Public availability:** 2026-10-14T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14423>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The October 14 new-submission batch and official schedule imply public availability at October 14 00:00 UTC, despite the October 10 submission date. Sections 2–6 and Appendices G–I cover 268 fitting experiments and three held-out runs; eight of nine held-out modality-loss predictions are within 2.6% of observed values.

**Limitations:** Coefficients depend on tokenizers, discrete next-token objectives, data quality and sparse architecture. The non-text-heavy continuation underpredicts text loss by 6.73%; larger-scale and video validation remain future work. Loss prediction is not a downstream-capability guarantee, and no code release or independent reproduction was verified.

## [2026-10-13](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-13.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Overcoming Data Imbalances with Expert Selection Biases](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13370>)

COAX adds category-dependent biases to expert selection during pretraining, giving scarce languages or modalities a larger preferred expert pool while keeping the number of active experts per token fixed. This supplies a simple capacity-allocation control for imbalanced training mixtures, with most multilingual and multimodal loss gains retained after removing the bias for standard inference.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:31.851Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Mixture of Experts, Multilingual Training, Capacity Allocation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13370>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the October 12 new-submission batch, with availability inferred using the official schedule. Sections 3–6 and Appendices B, F and G compare matched MoEs up to 10.6B total parameters, routing alternatives and data upsampling; seven-minority-language validation loss improves 0.286% relative in the largest eight-language setup.

**Limitations:** Most evidence concerns held-out next-token loss; multilingual task benchmarks are inconclusive and free generation remains undertrained. Some domains regress without inference-time bias. Training overhead ranges from about 20% at the smallest scale to 1.3%–2.4% in tested large/coarse configurations; no public implementation was verified.

## [2026-10-12](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-12.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12582>)

Elastic Latent Recurrence combines gated state updates, mixed loop counts within optimizer updates, and loop conditioning so one model can serve several inference depths while preserving competitive one-loop accuracy. Late mixed-depth training and cache reuse make this a practical recipe for trading additional computation for stronger answers within a fixed model footprint.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:07:12Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Recurrent Depth, Pretraining, Test-Time Compute

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12582>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–6 include matched-data 4B and 30B-A3B experiments: one-loop ten-task averages differ from non-recurrent baselines by -0.52/+1.04 points, and four loops improve over one loop by 7.25/4.75 points. Ablations isolate the training choices. The October 12 new-submission listing and official schedule imply October 12 00:00 UTC public announcement; this is inferred timing, distinct from the October 8 receipt date.

**Limitations:** Additional loops increase computation and latency. The 16% training overhead is a layer-execution estimate; Koi-4B has no matched non-recurrent control, and its AA scores are author-harness estimates. Last-loop caching changes attention semantics and retains separate GDP state. No released implementation or weights were verified.

## [2026-10-12](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-12.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Multi-Stream Attention Residuals](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630>)

MSAR lets each layer retrieve earlier representations through several contextual views created by causal convolutions, then combines those views into one layer input. Its blockwise design stores a single stream of source summaries while improving pretraining results in the tested MoE models, offering an alternative to fixed residual addition and single-stream depth attention.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:07:12Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Residual Architecture, MoE, Scaling Laws

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–4 compare 18B/28B MoE models across 12 tasks; averages rise from AttnRes's 41.8/49.4 to 45.7/52.4. Four-scale fits estimate a 1.58x iso-loss compute advantage over standard residuals. The October 12 new listing and official schedule imply October 12 00:00 UTC public availability, distinct from the October 9 receipt date.

**Limitations:** The compute advantage is fitted, not measured wall-clock speedup; training-token budgets are omitted in the appendix tables. FLOPs estimates exclude recomputation and optimizer updates, and no multi-seed uncertainty is reported. Source-storage savings do not remove all intermediate memory traffic. The linked project failed to load twice, so code was not verified.

## [2026-10-07](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-07.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [DeltaTTT: Layerwise Optimization for Nonlinear Recurrent Memory](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08553>)

DeltaTTT trains a nonlinear recurrent memory through separate local delta-rule objectives for its two layers, with chunkwise computation that preserves their tokenwise updates. The design improves the tested recurrent models' context use while retaining a compact memory state, offering an alternative between linear memory and full attention.

**Published:** 2026-10-06 · **First seen:** 2026-10-07T10:04:34Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Recurrent Memory, Test-Time Training, Delta Rule

**Public availability:** 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08553>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Roughly 0.5B models share 92.5B training tokens and 32K sequences. In the LaCT backbone, mean single-needle retrieval rises from 37.87 to 50.47; training throughput is 1.37 times the full-attention reference with 0.69 times its reserved memory. Original v1: 2026-10-06T15:40:06Z; verified October 7 new-submission batch.

**Limitations:** Full attention still reaches 72.42 on the retrieval aggregate and lower held-out loss. DeltaNet is faster and uses less memory than DeltaTTT. Experiments use a two-layer memory and 512-token sliding attention at modest model scale; no author implementation or independent reproduction was verified.

## [2026-10-06](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-06.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05978>)

This study compares flat byte-level and subword language models through scaling experiments, fine-grained tasks, and interventions on learned local representations. It shows that byte models' advantages at matched parameter counts coexist with a compute disadvantage, helping practitioners distinguish tokenization benefits from extra computation and choose where byte-level modeling is useful.

**Published:** 2026-10-05 · **First seen:** 2026-10-06T10:03:05Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Byte Models, Scaling Laws, Tokenization

**Public availability:** 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05978>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The 200M–3B task suite shows consistent word-manipulation and OCR gains, while the separate IsoFLOPs sweep favors subword models at matched training compute. Frozen layer interventions probe local aggregation. Original submission: 2026-10-05T08:29:08Z; October 6's listing and announcement schedule establish public availability at 00:00Z.

**Limitations:** Byte recipes also change training scheduling, hashed embeddings, and convolution width, so the comparison is not an isolated tokenizer swap. Results concern the tested hybrid backbones and scales. Speculative-decoding acceptance is simulated on reference text: the reported token-count multiplier is not measured end-to-end speedup. No author implementation was verified.

## [2026-10-02](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-02.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02193>)

HC-DLM couples a continuous latent plan with repeatedly decoded tokens that guide the next denoising step, allowing token decisions to be revised throughout generation. The design improves controlled planning and reasoning tasks at small scale, offering evidence that latent planning and token-level feedback can complement one another in diffusion models.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:32:39Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Diffusion Language Models, Latent Reasoning, Model Architecture

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02193>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Component ablations and matched 6M-parameter comparisons support the coupling: hard-Sudoku accuracy is 72.41% versus 70.73% for reproduced CCDD, and longer Countdown improves from 25.35% to 37.52%. A separate 118M sampling-model experiment evaluates short unconditional text. arXiv v1: 2026-10-01T17:59:39Z. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv cs.CL listing separately confirms the October 2 public announcement batch.

**Limitations:** Evidence remains at moderate scale; reported sampling parameter counts exclude embeddings and the training-only encoder. Natural-language comparisons use external-model generative perplexity, different tokenizers, and historical baselines; the autoregressive baseline still scores better, and reported training times are not hardware-controlled speed comparisons.

## [2026-10-01](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-01.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40295>)

The authors train hundreds of small language models on mixtures of human and detector-labeled AI web text, then fit scaling laws that distinguish AI text's saturating benefit from its potential harm. The results motivate tracking human and AI validation losses separately and choosing data mixtures according to the target distribution and available human data.

**Published:** 2026-09-30 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:32:39Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Scaling Laws, Pretraining Data, Synthetic Data

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40295>) · [Code](<https://github.com/pangramlabs/WildAI>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Across 800 runs from 19.9M to 973M parameters, the paper tests data-budget and mixture effects and extrapolates fits from models up to 268M. Its fitted law predicts held-out human-text loss better than the compared laws. arXiv v1: 2026-09-30T17:50:22Z, within this report's interval. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv recent-submissions listing separately confirms the October 1 public announcement batch.

**Limitations:** English web pretraining and next-token loss dominate the evidence; detection labels can be imperfect and the authors include detector-company researchers. Results do not establish that curated synthetic data or frontier-scale models follow the same tradeoff; forecast compute penalties are model-based projections.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653>)

Kimi K3 combines hybrid recurrent and latent attention, attention across residual layers, and a sparse expert architecture in a native multimodal model with 2.8 trillion total parameters and 104 billion activated parameters. Its public report connects architecture, data, optimization, and long-context post-training, providing a current reference for how several efficiency improvements support scaling a large open-weight model.

**Published:** 2026-07-27 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** MoE, Hybrid Attention, Scaling Laws, Multimodal

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The August 7 revision includes architecture equations, scaling-law experiments, training schedules, and evaluation settings; Section 3.2 reports approximately 2.5x overall scaling efficiency relative to Kimi K2 on held-out validation data.

**Limitations:** The efficiency result combines multiple changes and is not an isolated architectural gain; the authors state that overall performance trails their strongest proprietary comparators, and released weights do not make the full training process reproducible.
